questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the domain of the function $f \left(x\right) = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{x^{2} - 4x + 2}{x^{2} + 3}\right)is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f \left(x\right) = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{x^{2} - 4x + 2}{x^{2} + 3}\right)

We know that domain of~$\cos^{- 1}$\text{is} \left[-$1, 1\right]$

So,~\left|$\dfrac{x^{2} + 4x + 2}{x^{2} + 3}\right| \le1$

$⇒ \left($x^{2} - 4x + 2\right)2 $\le \left($x^{2} + 3\right)2$

$⇒ \left($x^{2} - 4x + 2\right)2 - \left($x^{2} + 3\right)2 ≤ 0$

$⇒ \left($2x^{2} - 4x + 5\right)\left(-$4x - 1\right) ≤ 0$

Since~\left($2x^{2} - 4x + 5\right) > 0$~as its discriminant~$D < 0$

So,~$- 4x - 1 \le 0 ⇒ x \ge - \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ x \in [ - \dfrac{1}{4}, \infty )

$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be a function such that $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x^{2} + 2x + 1}{x^{2} + 1}$. Then
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{x^{2} + 2x + 1}{x^{2} + 1}$

$f^{'} ( x ) = \dfrac{\left(x^{2} + 1\right) ( 2x + 2 ) - ( x^{2} + 2x + 1 ) 2x}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)2}$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) = \dfrac{2x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 2x + 2 - 2x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 2x}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)2}$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) = \dfrac{2 ( 1 - x^{2} )}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)2} = - \dfrac{2 ( x + 1 ) ( x - 1 )}{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)2}$

Clearly~$f ( x )$~is one-one in~ \left(- \infty , - 1\right)$~and also in~$( 1, \infty )$~but~$f ( x )$~is not one-one in~ \left(- \infty , \infty\right)$

$⇒ {α}^{2} + {β}^{3} = \left(-5\right)2 + \left(5\right)3$

questions.q: If& $f \left(x\right) = x^{3} - x^{2}f^{'}  \left($1\right) + xf^{"}\left($2\right) - f^{' ' '}\left($3\right)$,~$x \in R$, then$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let

$f\left(x\right) = x^{3} - ax^{2} + bx - c$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = 3x^{2} - 2ax + b$

$f^{"}\left(x\right) = 6x - 2a$

$f^{' ' '}\left(x\right) = 6$

Also,

$f^{'}\left(1\right) = a$

$⇒ 3 - 2a + b = a$

$⇒ 3a = b + 3$

Also,

$f^{"}\left(2\right) = 12 - 2a = b$

$⇒ 12 - 2a = 3a - 3$

$⇒ 5a = 15 ⇒ a = 3$

$⇒ b = 6$

And,

$f^{' ' '}\left(3\right) = c ⇒ c = 6$

Hence,

$f\left(x\right) = x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 6x - 6$

Now,

$f\left(3\right) + 2f\left(0\right) = 27 - 27 + 18 - 6 - 12 = 0$

$f\left(2\right) + f\left(1\right) = 8 - 12 + 12 - 6 + 1 - 3 + 6 - 6 = 0$

So,

$f \left(3\right) + 2f \left($0\right) = f \left(2\right) + f\left(1\right)$

$⇒2f \left(0\right) - f \left(1\right) + f \left($3\right) = $f\left($2\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & f_1(x)=\log _5\left(18 x-x^2-77\right) \\ & \therefore \quad 18 x-x^2-77 \gt 0 \\ & \quad x^2-18 x+77 \lt 0 \\ & x \in(7,11) \\ & \alpha=7, \beta=11 \\ & f_2(x)=\log _{(x-1)}\left(\frac{2 x^2+3 x-2}{x^2-3 x-4}\right) \\ & x \gt 1, x-1 \neq 1, \frac{2 x^2+3 x-2}{x^2-3 x-4} \gt 0 \\ & x \gt 1, x \neq 2, \frac{(2 x-1)(x+2)}{(x-4)(x+1)} \gt 0\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad x \in(4, \infty) \\ & \therefore \quad \gamma=4 \\ & \therefore \quad \alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=49+121+16 \\ & =186 \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics

$f\left(g\left(2k + 1\right)\right) = f\left(2k + 2\right) = k + 1$

$∴ f ( g ( x ) )$ is onto.

questions.q: If& $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{22x}{{2}^{2x} + 2}$,~$x \in R$, then $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2023}\right) + f  \left(\dfrac{2}{2023}\right) +$f \left(\dfrac{3}{2023}\right) . . . . . . . . . f\left(\dfrac{2022}{2023}\right)$& is equal to& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{22x}{{2}^{2x} + 2}$,

so~$f\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{22 - 2x}{{2}^{2 - 2x} + 2} = \dfrac{22}{{2}^{2} + {2}^{2x + 1}} = \dfrac{2}{2 + {2}^{2x}}$

Now~$f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{22x}{{2}^{2x} + 2} + \dfrac{2}{2 + {2}^{2x}} = 1$

So by using the relation~$f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = 1$~we will solve the given equation~

$f\left(\dfrac{1}{2023}\right) + f \left(\dfrac{2}{2023}\right) +$f \left(\dfrac{3}{2023}\right) . . . . . . . . . f\left(\dfrac{2022}{2023}\right)$

$= f\left(\dfrac{1}{2023}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2022}{2023}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2}{2023}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2021}{2023}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{3}{2023}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{2020}{2023}\right) . . . . . . . . . f \left(\dfrac{1011}{2023}\right) +f \left(\dfrac{1012}{2023}\right)

$= \mathop{f \left(\dfrac{1}{2023}\right) +$f \left(\dfrac{2022}{2023}\right)$⏟}_{1} + \mathop{f \left(\dfrac{2}{2023}\right) +$f \left(\dfrac{2021}{2023}\right)$⏟}_{1} + \mathop{f \left(\dfrac{3}{2023}\right) +$f \left(\dfrac{2020}{2023}\right)$⏟}_{1} . . . . . . . . . + \$mathop{f \left(\dfrac{1011}{2023}\right) +f \left(\dfrac{1012}{2023}\right)⏟}_{1}$

$= 1 + 1 + 1 . . . . . . . . . 1011\text{times} =1011$

questions.q: The function $f: N - { 1 } \to N$; defined by $f\left(n\right) =$ the highest prime factor of $n$, is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $f: N - { 1 } \to N$

$f ( n ) =$ The highest prime factor of $n$.

Since, the only prime factor of $2$ is $2$.

$⇒ f ( 2 ) = 2$

Also, factors of $4$ are $1, 2\text{and}4$. Out of these, the highest prime factor is $2$.

$⇒ f ( 4 ) = 2$

Similarly the highest prime factor of $16, 32, 64, 128, . . .$ is $2$

So, the given function is many one.

Now, no composite number will be image of any number.

Example: $4$ is not image of any element

So, the given function $f \left(x\right) is into.

Hence many one and into

Or, neither one-one nor onto.

$

questions.q: $The domain of the function $\cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2\sin^{- 1}  \left(\dfrac{1}{4x^{2} - 1}\right)}{π}\right)$ \text{ and }  is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f \left(x\right) = \cos^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{2\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4x^{2} - 1}\right)}{π}\right)

Case I:~$- 1 $\le \dfrac{1}{4x^{2} - 1} \le$1$

$⇒ 4x^{2} - 1 ≥ 1$~or $4x^{2} - 1 $\le -$1$ and $4x^{2} - 1 \ne 0$

$∴ x^{2} $\ge \dfrac{1}{2}~or $x^{2} ≤ 0 ⇒ x = 0$~and $x \ne $\pm \dfrac{1}{2}

$∴ x \in \left(- \infty , - \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$\cup \left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$\cup \left\{0\right\}$

Case II:~$- 1 $\le \dfrac{2\sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4x^{2} - 1}\right)}{π} \le$1$

$⇒ - $\dfrac{π}{2} \le \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{4x^{2} - 1}\right) \le \dfrac{π}{2}~which is always true.

Hence,~$x \in \left(- \infty , - \dfrac{1}{2}\right]$\cup \left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$\cup \left\{0\right\}$

$

Let $g: N \to N$ be defined as

$g ( 3n + 1 ) = 3n + 2$

$g ( 3n + 2 ) = 3n + 3$

$g ( 3n + 3 ) = 3n + 1$, for all $n \ge 0$

Then which of the following statements is true ?
options: There exists an onto function $f: N \to N$ such that $fog = f$

There exists a one-one function $f: N \to N$ such
that~$fog = f$
There exists a function $f: N \to N$ such that~$gof = f$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$g: N \to N$

$g ( 3n + 1 ) = 3n + 2$

$g ( 3n + 2 ) = 3n + 3$

$g ( 3n + 3 ) = 3n + 1$

$g\left(x\right) = \left\{
x + 1; x = 3k + 1
x + 1;x = 3k + 2
x - 2;x = 3k + 3
\right$

$g\left(g\left(x\right)\right) = \left\{
x + 2; x = 3k + 1
x - 1;x = 3k + 2
x - 1;x = 3k + 3
\right$

$g\left(g\left(g\left(x\right)\right)\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}x; & x = 3k + 1 \\ x; & x = 3k + 2 \\ x; & x = 3k + 3\end{cases}$\right$

If $f: N \to N, f$ is a one-one function such that~$f ( g ( x ) ) = f ( x ) ⇒ g ( x ) = x$, which is not the case

If $f: N \to N, f$ is an onto function such that $f ( g ( x ) ) = f ( x )$~one possibility is

$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}n; & x = 3n + 1 \\ n; & x = 3n + 2 \\ n; & x = 3n + 3\end{cases}$\right; n \in N$

Here $f \left(x\right)$ is onto, also $f ( g ( x ) ) = f ( x ) \forall x \in N

$

questions.q: Let $R = { a, b, c, d, e }$~and $S = { 1, 2, 3, 4 }$. Total number of onto functions $f: R \to S$ such that $f ( a ) \ne 1$, is equal to ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$R = { a, b, c, d, e }$~and $S = { 1, 2, 3, 4 }$

Now taking,~$f ( a ) = 1$~we get,~one of $f ( b ) , f ( c ) , f ( d ) , f ( e ) = 1$~then total such cases $= 4 \cdot 3 ! = 24$
Now if,~only $f ( a ) = 1$, then we have distribute~\left\{2, 3, 4\right\}$~amongst~\left\{b, c, d, e\right\}$,
So, total cases $= {3}^{4} - \left(C1 3 \cdot {2}^{4}\right) + \left($C2 3 \cdot1\right)$
$= 36$
So, number~of onto functions when $f ( a ) = 1$~is $24 + 36 = 60$

Now finding, total number~of onto functions,
$= {4}^{5} - \left(C1 4 \cdot {3}^{5}\right) + \left($C2 4 $\cdot {2}^{5}\right) - \left($C3 4 $\cdot$1\right)$
$= 1024 - 973 + 192 - 4$
$= 240$
Number of required functions when~f\left($a\right) \ne 1$~will be,

$= 240 - 60= 180$

questions.q: $Let $f: R \to R$~be a function defined $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2e^{2x}}{e^{2x} + e}$.~Then $f\left(\dfrac{1}{100}\right) +f  \left(\dfrac{2}{100}\right) +f \$left(\dfrac{3}{100}\right) + \ldots ++$f\left(\dfrac{99}{100}\right)$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{2e^{2x}}{e^{2x} + e}$

$f\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{2e^{2\left(1 - x\right)}}{e^{2\left(1 - x\right)} + e} = \dfrac{2e}{e + e^{2x}}$

Now,~$f\left(x\right) + f\left(1 - x\right) = 2$~

i.e.~$f\left(\dfrac{1}{100}\right) + f\left(\dfrac{99}{100}\right) = 2$

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{100}\right) + f \left(\dfrac{2}{100}\right) + ...f \left(\dfrac{99}{100}\right) =$2 $\times$49 + $f\left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)

$= 98 + 1 = 99$

$

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$~be a function defined by $f\left(x\right) = \left(2\left(1 - \dfrac{x25}{2}\right)\left(2 + x^{25}\right)\right)\dfrac{1}{50}$. If the function $g\left(x\right) = f \left(f \left(f  \left(x\right)\right)\right) + $f\l$left(f\left($x\right))$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $g  \left($1\right)$& is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given& $f\left(x\right) = \left[2\left(1 - \dfrac{x25}{2}\right)\left(2 + x^{25}\right)\right]\dfrac{1}{50}$

$f\left(x\right) = \left[\left(2 - x^{25}\right)\left(2 + x^{25}\right)\right]\dfrac{1}{50}$

$= \left(4 - x^{50}\right)\dfrac{1}{50}$

i.e.~$f\left(f\left(x\right)\right) = \left(4 - \left(\left(4 - x^{50}\right)\dfrac{1}{50}\right)50\right)\dfrac{1}{50} = x$

Now~$g\left(x\right) = f \left(f \left(f \left(x\right)\right)\right) + $f\l$left(f\left($x\right))$

=f\left($x\right) + x$

So~g\left($1\right) = $f\left($1\right) + 1 = $3\dfrac{1}{50} +$1$

Hence~\lleft[g\left(1\right)] = $\$lleft[3\dfrac{1}{50} +$1] = 2

$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7\right\} .$ Then the number of possible functions $f: S \to S$ such that $f \left(m \cdotn\right) = f  \left($m\right)$\cdotf  \left(n\right)$~for every $m, n \in S$ and $m \cdotn \in S$, is equal to _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given,

$f \left(mn\right) = f \left($m\right)$\cdotf \left(n\right)$

Put~$m = 1,$~then~f \left($1 \cdotn\right) = f \left(1\right)$\cdotf\left($n\right) ⇒ $f\left($1\right) = $1\left\{f\left($n\right) \ne 0\right\}

Put~$m = n = 2$

$f \left($4\right) = f \left(2\right) \cdot f\left(2\right)$

If~$f\left(2\right) = 1,$~then~$f\left(4\right) = 1$~and if~$f\left(2\right) = 2,$~then~$f \left(4\right) = 4$

Put~$m = 2, n = 3$

$f\left(6\right) = f\left(2\right)\$cdotf\left($3\right)$

If~$f \left($2\right) = 1,$~then~f\left($3\right)$~can be any value between~$1$~to~$7$

If~$f \left($2\right) = 2,$~then~$f\left($3\right)$~can be~$1$~or~$2$~or~$3$

Similarly~$f \left(5\right), f \left(7\right)$~can take any value from~\left\{1, 2, . . . , 7\right\}$

So, total number of function~$= \left(1 \times1 \times7 \times1 \times7 \times1 \times7\right) + \left(1 \times1 \times3 \times1 \times7 \times1 \times7\right)$

$= 490

$
